readerTitle: The painting job both sides wanted, and nobody got
caseNote: 가상 사례 (외벽 도장업자와 집주인, 기장 대행 회사와 물류 회사) · 모든 수치는 설명용
insight: 협상은 가격 싸움이 아니라 두 사람의 보이지 않는 한계선이 겹치는 구간을 찾는 일이다. 겹치는 구간이 없으면 말솜씨가 아니라 거래 내용을 바꿔야 한다.
misconception: 제시 가격과 희망 가격의 차이가 곧 협상 범위이고, 협상을 잘하면 어떤 차이든 좁힐 수 있다.

sources.text: 협상론의 표준 개념 (zone of possible agreement, ZOPA). Raiffa, H. (1982). The Art and Science of Negotiation. Harvard University Press.

factChecks.note: ZOPA 개념의 출처로 Raiffa(1982)를 적었습니다. 이 책에서 'zone of agreement' 개념을 다루는지, 해당 용어를 처음 쓴 문헌이 무엇인지 게시 전에 확인하세요. 카드 본문에는 인명을 넣지 않았습니다.
도장 사례 계산: 도장업자 하한 $3,000, 집주인 상한 $3,500 → 합의 가능 구간 $3,000~$3,500. 제시가 $4,000과 집주인 희망가 $2,800은 모두 구간 밖. 즉시 $3,000으로 내리면 최대 $500(3,500 − 3,000)을 포기. 6번 카드의 가정: 집주인 상한 $2,500 < 하한 $3,000 → 구간 없음.
기장 대행 사례 계산: 하한 $1,800 > 고객 상한 $1,500 → 구간 없음. 중간값 $1,650은 고객 상한보다 높고 하한보다 낮음. 가벼운 패키지로 하한이 $1,300으로 내려가면 구간 $1,300~$1,500이 생기고 제안가 $1,450은 구간 안. 경쟁사 견적 $1,400보다는 높다는 점을 감안해도 고객 상한 이내.

cards.title: The painting job both sides wanted, and nobody got
body: A homeowner asks a painter to quote the outside of her house. He says $4,000. She'd hoped for about $2,800 and could stretch to $3,500. She says, "That's too much for us," and thanks him.
He would have taken $3,000. He says nothing and drives away.
Any price between $3,000 and $3,500 would have left both of them better off than no deal. Neither of them ever found out.

image.label: A painter's van leaving a house with a half-scraped wall
image.brief: 3D 클레이 스타일. 외벽 페인트가 군데군데 벗겨진 집 앞에서 도장업자의 밴이 떠나고, 현관에 선 집주인이 아쉬운 표정. 두 사람 머리 위에 각각 물음표가 담긴 말풍선. 실제 브랜드 로고는 쓰지 않음.

cards.title: You're the painter.
body: You quoted $4,000 to paint a house exterior. The lowest price you'd accept, after paint, labor and a fair profit, is $3,000.
The homeowner says, "That's more than we can do." What do you say next?

options.text: Drop to $3,000 right away to save the job
options.feedback: You might keep the job, but you give away everything between your floor and her limit. If she'd have paid $3,500, that's $500 gone in one sentence.

options.text: Ask what budget she had in mind and what matters most to her
options.feedback: You learn roughly where her limit sits before you move. That tells you whether a deal can exist and where to aim inside it.

options.text: Hold at $4,000 and explain why your work is worth it
options.feedback: Holding firm pays off if she's bluffing. But if her real limit is $3,500, no explanation reaches $4,000, and you both lose a deal you wanted.

cards.title: Line up the numbers.
body: The deal didn't fail because the gap was too big. It failed because nobody looked for the **overlap**.

breakdown.label: Painter's quote
breakdown.detail: His opening number, not his limit

breakdown.label: The overlap
breakdown.detail: Every price here beats no deal for both

cards.title: The zone of possible agreement
body: The **zone of possible agreement** is the range between the seller's lowest acceptable price and the buyer's highest. Negotiators often shorten it to ZOPA.
Inside the zone, any deal leaves both sides better off than walking away. Outside it, at least one side would rather walk.
Here the zone ran from $3,000 to $3,500. The $4,000 quote and the $2,800 hope both sat outside it, and together they hid it.

image.label: Two price ranges overlapping between $3,000 and $3,500
image.brief: 가로 가격 축($2,500~$4,500) 위에 막대 두 개. 위쪽 파란 막대 "Painter accepts: $3,000 and up", 아래쪽 주황 막대 "Homeowner pays: up to $3,500". 두 막대가 겹치는 $3,000~$3,500 구간을 초록색으로 강조하고 "Zone of possible agreement" 라벨.

cards.title: Every negotiation asks two questions.
body: It helps to split any negotiation into two separate questions.
list: **Is there a zone at all?** Each side's walk-away point decides this. Clever talking doesn't change it.
**Where inside the zone do we land?** Information, patience and the first numbers on the table decide this.
cards.callout: The catch: each side sees only its own limit. The other side's limit is a guess you have to test with questions.

cards.title: No overlap? Change the deal, not the pitch.
body: Say her limit were $2,500, not $3,500. Now no price works for both. Haggling harder only wastes an afternoon.
But the painter's $3,000 floor is for *this* job. Paint only the front and sides. Let her do the scraping. Book it in his slow month. Each change lowers his costs, and his floor with them.
Redesign the deal until a zone appears, or walk away politely.

image.label: Two ranges that don't overlap, then shift until they do
image.brief: 두 칸 비교 인포그래픽. 왼쪽: 파란 막대와 주황 막대 사이에 빈틈, "No zone". 오른쪽: 작업 범위를 줄여 파란 막대가 왼쪽으로 이동해 겹침이 생김, "Smaller job, new zone". 붓, 사다리 아이콘을 작게 곁들임.

cards.softwareNote: Software sellers do the same with fewer seats, an annual contract or a lighter support plan. Each lowers the cost of serving the customer, which can move the vendor's floor below the buyer's budget.

cards.title: The zone is a guess, and it moves.
body: Nobody shows you their real limit. "That's our max" might be true, or it might be a tactic. Treat the other side's limit as an estimate and keep testing it.
Zones also shift. A rival's quote, a looming deadline or a busy season can move either limit overnight.
And guard your own floor. Once the other side knows it, the deal tends to land right on it.

cards.title: Now it's a bookkeeping firm.
body: You offer monthly bookkeeping to small companies. For a local logistics firm, your floor is $1,800 a month, given the hours involved.
Their finance manager says $1,500 is the most she can approve, and a rival quoted $1,400. You believe the $1,500 is real. What do you do?

options.text: Propose meeting in the middle at $1,650
options.feedback: It feels fair, but it's above their limit and below yours. Splitting the difference only works inside a zone, and here there isn't one.

options.text: Offer a lighter package at $1,450: quarterly reports, with their staff uploading receipts, which cuts your floor to about $1,300
options.feedback: Less work for you moves your floor below their budget. You create a zone instead of arguing inside one that doesn't exist.
This protects your margins, and it's right if no version of the deal works. But you leave before checking whether a smaller deal could fit.

cards.title: Find the overlap before you fight over the price.
body: A deal can only happen where the seller's floor sits below the buyer's limit. Opening numbers hide that range. Questions reveal it, and changing the deal can create it.
**Try it today:** pick a deal you're working on. Write down your walk-away point and your best guess at theirs. Do they overlap? If not, what could you change?
